_note: The noticeboard on Market Square (docs/15-regions.md, Noticeboards; decision 0484). Kettle Notch's board.json is the model and its note holds here: the seed picks a writer's line and fills {where} from `spots` and {in} from `places`; `pay` is the least and most each kind may pay, in item worth, and `npm run check` holds every payment to it. Harlow pays about half as much again as Hardscrabble, for levels 14 to 18, and gear comes more often and Stout (one Sunday Best line). Hannah Corliss sets every notice, so the blurb says so; she doesn't write them. A writer keeps to one place at every hour, so the map's star is never wrong: Fessenden, the Squire and Gault on Market Square, Mrs. Kidder on Mill Street, Mother Peck in the Row boarding house. Abel Mudgett is on the lake by day and the mill rows at night, so his notice is a posted one. Lower Harlow is left out: it resets, and board work stays above ground. The Watcher isn't a board fight.
gearHint: There's a man at the Tankard with a month paid ahead who deals in that sort of thing. He'll tell you what it's worth. He'll tell you twice.

words.fightBlurb: A notice on the board in Market Square, from {name}, set by Hannah Corliss. Pays {pay}. Creatures already seen off come back after a rest.

posted.text: ORDINANCE. No singing in Market Square after ten o'clock at night. This applies to everyone. A. HATCH, J.P.
ICE, cut and put up, when the lake freezes. Not before. Not from round the steeple. A. MUDGETT
STAGE leaves Thursday. Not Wednesday. Not after dark. L. COBURN
MILL RUNNING. Hands wanted at noon. A. FRYE, for the mill office

notices.title: My Yardstick
notices.text: Lost my yardstick {where}. Brass at both ends. It was a yard when I dropped it. Bring it in before the cold gets at it.

notices.title: Twenty-Two Yards
notices.got: Twenty-two before fulling. It comes back shorter. That's what fulling is. Tell him.
notices.text: Take this bolt to Mrs. Kidder at the fulling mill. Twenty-two yards. I measured it twice. Ask her to measure it when it comes in.

writers.signed: A. Hatch, Justice of the Peace
thanks: Very good. I'll enter it in the record.
That will do. I'd thank you formally, but there's no form for it.

notices.title: Kid Gloves
notices.payWords: the Squire's kid gloves from the bench
notices.text: Kid gloves, for the bench. I wore them to be sworn in, and not since. See off two lots in {in} and they're yours.

notices.title: The Seal
notices.text: I have lost the seal of my office {where}. Brass, with the county on it. Until it's back, nothing I sign is so.

notices.title: After Ten
notices.text: Something in {in} carries on after ten at night. The ordinance stops at the square. I'd like it seen to all the same. Two lots.

thanks: Good. The horses'll be glad. They won't show it.
Obliged. The gray says so too, in his way.

notices.title: A Drummer's Boots
notices.text: A drummer left his boots at the stable and went on by the stage. He'd no use for them sitting down. See off two lots in {in} and they're yours.

notices.title: Past the Bars
notices.text: The horses won't go up {in} past the bars. Clear it, all of it, and I'll take the gray up and see.

at.words: at home on the mill rows, after dark
at home on the mill rows, after dark

thanks: Good. One thing in this town done when it was meant to be.
Thank you. Don't tell Penhallow it was quick. He'll want it quicker.
That's done. Mind the race on your way.

notices.title: Fulled Twice
notices.text: A coat went through the stocks twice by mistake. Wind won't go through it now, and nobody at the mill can get into it. See off two lots in {in} and it's yours.

notices.title: Race Ice
notices.text: Ice off {in} has been walking down into the race at night. Two lots, please. Mr. Penhallow wants the mill run till dark. It won't run with ice in the wheel either.

writers.signed: Mother Peck, the Row boarding house

at.words: upstairs at the Row boarding house, after dark
upstairs at the Row boarding house, after dark
at the stove in the Row boarding house

thanks: Good. Hands eat first. You're a hand today.
That's a help. Mind the step, it's greasy.

notices.title: The Stew Pot
notices.text: The curs on {in} had my stew pot over again. See off two lots. Hands eat first. Curs don't eat at all.

notices.title: Cheese for the Stew
notices.text: Wanted: two cheeses for the hands' stew. The rams on the Pasture Lane have been at the carts coming down. They've more cheese than I have.
